title: Predict the Reward, Not the World: World Reward Models for ML Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.38439v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Search-based machine-learning (ML) agents improve a solution by writing candidate programs, executing them, and keeping the best. Execution gives the search reliable feedback, but a single run can take hours, and most runs end in programs the agent discards. Recent agents try to save these runs by letting a large language model act as a world model that predicts how each program would perform. However, a wrong prediction feeds the search false information. We argue that an agent does not need to predict the outcome of execution, only the decision that execution would support. We propose World Reward Models (WRMs), which learn from real execution results to choose directly which candidate will perform better, without predicting any intermediate outcome. translated_title: 预测奖励，而非预测世界：面向机器学习智能体的世界奖励模型
translated_abstract: 基于搜索的机器学习（ML）智能体通过编写候选程序、执行这些程序并保留最佳者来不断改进解决方案。执行为搜索提供了可靠的反馈，但单次运行可能耗时数小时，而且大多数运行的最终程序会被智能体丢弃。最近的智能体尝试通过让大型语言模型充当世界模型来预测每个程序的表现，从而节省这些运行的开销。然而，错误的预测会向搜索提供虚假信息。我们认为，智能体并不需要预测执行的结果，而只需要预测执行所能支持的决策。我们提出了世界奖励模型（WRMs），它从真实的执行结果中学习，直接选择哪个候选程序表现更好，而无需预测任何中间结果。我们证明了一个从相同输入出发预测执行结果的选择器，其性能无法超越最佳的直接选择器；并且预测结果会引入额外的误差，可能使经过似然训练的（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出世界奖励模型（WRMs），让智能体直接从真实执行结果中学习选出更优的候选程序，而无需用世界模型预测执行结果，并从理论上证明直接选择器不会劣于任何基于预测的选择器。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes World Reward Models (WRMs), which learn directly from real execution results to choose the better candidate program without predicting any intermediate outcome, and proves that such direct selectors cannot be outperformed by prediction-based ones.
